verdicts.quote: There is an in-org bot entry point in Salesforce Lightning Experience. ... An authorized user on desktop Lightning Experience can open the bot from the Salesforce workspace.
verdicts.missing: Which Lightning surface hosts the bot (app/tab page, utility bar, record page component) and what context, if any, that surface passes in.

verdicts.quote: The bot does not fetch Salesforce record data to enrich a prompt. ... The provider-bound request contains no content drawn from that record by the bot.
The bot does not fetch Salesforce record data to enrich a prompt.
Every chat user requires an explicit bot access grant to send prompts. ... including a Salesforce admin who has setup rights only.
After one user signs out and another signs in on the same browser, the second user cannot read the first user's messages through the bot.
If Apex performs the callout, Grok cannot be reached from an Apex transaction with pending uncommitted writes.
verdicts.missing: Whether the callout runs synchronously or asynchronously (Queueable/future/batch); the design is left conditional.

verdicts.quote: The xAI credential is unavailable to the chat client. Inspection of the bot page, its ordinary client traffic, and its browser storage reveals no xAI credential.
verdicts.missing: Where the credential is stored (Named/External Credential is only conditional in C-77) and that it never appears in code or metadata.

verdicts.quote: If Apex performs the callout, an Apex transaction has at most 120 seconds of cumulative callout timeout.
verdicts.missing: CPU time limit and heap limit as such are not named; only callout timeout, count (100) and payload sizes are given.

verdicts.quote: If Salesforce has no applicable endpoint authorization for the Apex callout, a send produces a setup failure without reaching xAI.
Given two deliveries of the same successful completion, the originating chat shows a single answer for that send.
verdicts.missing: The mechanism by which the page learns a result arrived (platform event, polling, LMS, or inline return).

verdicts.quote: A repeated notification for one send produces at most one visible answer.
When xAI rejects the API authorization, the user sees that administrator intervention is needed for setup.
When the configured xAI team or model reaches a rate cap and xAI returns HTTP 429, the user sees a throttling outcome with guidance to try later.
If Grok reports an incomplete result, such as reaching its output token limit, the bot reports a failed attempt due to incomplete generation.
The bot does not create a persistent chat transcript in Salesforce.
verdicts.missing: The shape of whatever is stored (diagnostic/send records): fields, status, timestamps, model identifier, usage counts.

verdicts.quote: After a successful conversation, an authorized admin inspecting the bot's stored Salesforce data finds no saved prompt or answer transcript.
The bot sends no Salesforce user identifiers in inference content unless the user supplies them as chat text.
the next provider request uses the longest fitting suffix of complete exchanges in chronological order, with the full latest prompt.
In an empty chat with working setup, a nonblank prompt of exactly the displayed maximum length reaches Grok in full.
An authorized Salesforce admin can disable new Grok sends for the org.
Diagnostic availability has a documented lifetime.
verdicts.missing: Whether any record of who asked and when is kept for successful sends, and the retention period value.

verdicts.quote: A future deployment that packages Salesforce external credentials still needs the secret provisioned for the target org.
Each send has a finite, published wait deadline.
verdicts.missing: The actual latency bound / deadline value.

verdicts.quote: A Salesforce user without a bot grant ... can tell that bot access is required.
Existing Salesforce records retain their pre-installation values when the bot is introduced.
